newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Rugby union-Injury to Little opens door for McLeod.
newsitem.headline: Rugby union-Injury to Little opens door for McLeod.

text.p: HAMILTON, May 7 - Waikato rugby coach John Boe believes second five-eighths Scott McLeod might get an All Black test recall this season because of an injury to Chiefs Super 12 team-mate Walter Little.
McLeod made his All Black debut last year at the expense of an injured Little but was relegated to the reserves when the North Harbour player regained fitness.

Yesterday Little ruled himself out of rugby for at least six weeks because of recurring knee trouble, which means he will miss the All Blacks trials, the one-off test against Fiji and the two internationals against Argentina.
Little may also be struggling for match fitness when the All Blacks play the first Bledisloe Cup test against Australia in Christchurch on July 3.
Canterbury's Mark Mayerhofler, Wellington's Jason O'Halloran and Auckland's Lee Stensness are all showing good form in Super 12 to be ranked as contenders alongside McLeod.
However Boe, who is also backs coach for the Super 12 Chiefs, believes McLeod has an edge over his rivals.
"Scott is bigger in stature which is a plus for him. He is big and strong and off-loads the ball in the tackle."
Boe was critical of McLeod's efforts for the All Blacks last season but believes the experience has matured him.
"I thought his game went backwards when he made the All Blacks. It was because so much had happened to him in such a short time. I think his feet left the ground a bit fast."
Little, New Zealand's most-capped second-five with 44 tests, told coach John Hart yesterday he needed a break so that his left knee could heal.
Little has been told he needs to build up the muscles round the damaged anterior cruciate ligament. He will reassess his progress in about six weeks.
Hart said Little's absence would have a "significant" impact on the All Blacks.
"He is a proven player at the hardest and highest level. To step into his shoes is not an easy task."
Hart said he wanted a second-five who was both an attacking and defensive player, with the ability to hit the line and feed outside, freeing up space for others in the backline.
Little first injured the knee in a club match in Tokoroa in 1986 and it has plagued him ever since, reducing his effectiveness during this season's Super 12.
"It's been an on-going injury and he has shown a lot of courage playing while we were without cover because of Scott's (back) injury," said Boe.
McLeod returned to rugby in the Chiefs' win over the Gauteng Lions at Rugby Park in Hamilton on Saturday night.
